country.name: China
country.kicker: An old civilization. A modern transformation.

overview.summary: A vast, diverse country reshaped by rapid industrialization and urban growth. China’s enormous domestic market and deep manufacturing networks make its choices consequential far beyond its borders.
overview.geography: China stretches from high plateaus and deserts in the west to densely settled plains and river valleys in the east. Its eastern coast opens onto the Pacific trading system.

whyItMatters.title: Inside the world’s supply chains
whyItMatters.text: From everyday goods to batteries and industrial equipment, production networks connect Chinese factories to customers worldwide.

whyItMatters.title: Scale changes the stakes
whyItMatters.text: Its energy use, aging population, and development choices have global economic and environmental consequences.

stories.question: How did China become a manufacturing center?
stories.summary: The transformation happened through decades of experimentation and investment.

sections.title: Reform in stages
sections.text: Reform and opening up began in 1978. Changes first reshaped rural incentives, then expanded opportunities for enterprise, investment, and trade.

sections.title: Networks build on networks
sections.text: Coastal cities connected labor, ports, roads, and suppliers. As skills and infrastructure grew, manufacturing extended into more complex industries. Low wages alone cannot explain that system.

stories.takeaway: Manufacturing strength lives in an ecosystem of suppliers, infrastructure, and accumulated knowledge.

scene.mapNote: Coastal access helped connect reform-era industry to world markets.

stories.question: Why is the east so much more densely populated?
stories.summary: Climate, terrain, and water help explain a striking imbalance.

sections.title: Land that supports settlement
sections.text: Eastern plains and major river basins offered conditions for intensive farming and large settlements. Western deserts and highlands present different constraints.

sections.title: Old patterns meet new opportunities
sections.text: Modern jobs and transport reinforce some historic concentrations. This does not make the west empty: it contains diverse communities, cities, and strategic resources.

stories.takeaway: National averages hide enormous differences in the places people actually inhabit.

scene.mapNote: Compare the broad western highlands with the eastern river plains.

stories.question: What did opening up actually change?
stories.summary: A familiar date, 1978, marks the start of a process rather than a single switch.

sections.title: Learning through experiments
sections.text: Local trials and special economic zones tested ways to attract investment and organize production before policies spread more widely.

sections.title: A transformation with new pressures
sections.text: Rising incomes and urbanization came alongside uneven opportunities, environmental costs, and reliance on investment. An aging population adds another challenge.

stories.takeaway: China’s recent history is a sequence of institutional choices and adjustments, not an automatic result of size.

scene.mapNote: Southern coastal experiments became gateways to the world economy.
